r-surface-floating.$description: A menu is a small card in this identity, so it keeps the card corner.

r-control.$description: The brief's button corner. The radius scale has no 8, so this is a literal.

r-control-sm.$description: Checkbox and segment, one step under the button.

r-field.$description: A field matches the button it sits beside.

r-marker.$description: Status pills and badges are fully round, as the brief draws them.

r-media.$description: A photo takes the corner of the card that holds it.

aspect-media.$description: Width over height: 3:2 landscape for covers, dishes and frozen maps.

fit-media.$description: Photos fill their frame; a parcel photo is evidence, not composition.

overlay-media.$description: The page closing over a picture, which here is paper.

fw-heading.$description: The brief writes every title at 600.

track-heading.$description: The nearest step to the brief's -0.03em on large titles.

lh-prose.$description: Reads well at 15px and clears the 1.5 floor.

lh-heading.$description: The brief's 1.04 falls under the floor of 1; this is the nearest legal step.

ff-eyebrow.$description: The brief's eyebrow is IBM Plex Mono, which is what makes it read as a system label.

ff-label.$description: Field labels stay in the interface face.

fw-eyebrow.$description: The eyebrow is small and uppercase; 500 is enough weight.

fw-control.$description: A button label carries the same weight as a title.

tt-eyebrow.$description: The brief's mono eyebrow is set in capitals.

tt-label.$description: A tool read with one hand in the sun does not shout at the person reading it.

track-eyebrow.$description: The brief's 0.14em on uppercase mono labels.

track-label.$description: Sentence-case labels need no extra tracking.

track-trail.$description: A crumb takes ff-label, which here is Archivo in sentence case, so the mono tracking the role is born at only loosens a proportional face.

step-label.$description: Capitals and tracking are what make a 10px label read as a system label, and this identity gives up both: ff-label is Archivo, tt-label is none, track-label is normal. The step is what is left to carry the register, so a column header sits at the eyebrow's 11px and stays legible on a phone held in the sun.

step-trail.$description: A crumb is chrome a reader passes on the way to the title, which is the 12px the brief spends on secondary control text.

step-title-surface.$description: The brief's 17px section name. Safe because the fs ladder is not re-answered.

step-title-section.$description: One rung under the screen title.

step-title-page.$description: The brief's 28px screen title; no fs step is 28.

step-title-hero.$description: The public landing is the only place a hero is drawn.

pad-control-y.$description: Height comes from density; this is the ink inside it.

gap-control.$description: An icon beside its label, and nothing else.

grid-min.$description: A merchant card with a 3:2 cover and two lines of text.

container-max.$description: The width of the brief's own canvas.

pad-surface-head.$description: The air the head keeps over the rule under it. One step under the card's own padding, which lands it against the 18px above the eyebrow and reads as a head with room rather than a caption stuck to a line.

fill-surface.$description: White is reserved for cards, so the card is base-200 and the page is base-100.

fill-surface-floating.$description: A floating surface is the same card.

fill-surface-sunken.$description: A well inside a white card is paper.

fill-field.$description: A field sits on the card and shares its ground.

fill-hover.$description: A hovered row drops to paper.

fill-track.$description: Progress tracks and table heads take the hairline colour.

ink-body.$description: Ink, held back by its level.

ink-eyebrow.$description: The brief's eyebrows are grey; an accent spent here is the accent the primary action was saving.

ink-muted.$description: Ink, held further back by its level.

edge-surface-floating.$description: With every shadow at zero, an ink hairline is what separates a menu from the card under it.

bw-surface.$description: One pixel. The brief expresses every edge at this width.

bw-surface-head.$description: One pixel, like every other edge here. With every shadow at zero the hairline is the only thing this identity has to say that a head is chrome and what follows it is content, and a panel of dense rows is exactly where that has to be said.

bw-control.$description: One pixel. The brief expresses every edge at this width.

bw-field.$description: One pixel. The brief expresses every edge at this width.

bw-separator.$description: One pixel. The brief expresses every edge at this width.

bw-marker.$description: One pixel. The brief expresses every edge at this width.

shadow-surface-floating.$description: The brief has no shadow anywhere; depth is the hairline border.

shadow-surface-rest.$description: The brief has no shadow anywhere; depth is the hairline border.

shadow-surface-deep.$description: The brief has no shadow anywhere; depth is the hairline border.

shadow-control-raised.$description: The brief has no shadow anywhere; depth is the hairline border.

shadow-control-rest.$description: The brief has no shadow anywhere; depth is the hairline border.

lift-control.$description: Nothing rises on hover; depth is borders.

dur-state.$description: A state change is visible without being slow.

ease-hover.$description: Out, so the end of the move is the calm part.

ease-state.$description: The same curve, so nothing on screen moves two ways.

press-scale.$description: The one gesture this identity permits.

rhythm-component.$description: A card and the next card.

rhythm-section.$description: Between two sections; dense enough to scan a panel on a phone.
